title: Cat grooming market in Bangalore
prompt: Estimate the annual market size (in ₹) of professional cat grooming services in Bangalore.

hints.label: Average household size in Indian metros
Share of urban Indian households that own any pet
Dog vs cat split among pet-owning households
hints.value: dogs are roughly 3x as common as cats

hints.label: Share of pet owners who use paid grooming at all
hints.value: a minority, mostly in higher-income homes

hints.label: Typical home-visit grooming session price (cat)
hints.value: ₹800 to ₹2,000 depending on coat and service

hints.label: Number of pet clinics in Bangalore
Share of Bangalore households in top income bracket
Typical cat adoption price
hints.value: ₹5,000 to ₹30,000 for breeds, free for strays

hints.label: Monthly pet food spend per cat
Number of pet grooming salons in Bangalore
hints.value: a few hundred, many of them dog focused

hints.label: Long-haired breeds share of pet cats

steps.title: Households in Bangalore
steps.explain: Start from population and household size. 1.4 crore people at 4 per household.

steps.title: Cat-owning households
steps.explain: About 1 in 6 households has a pet. Dogs outnumber cats about 3 to 1, so cats are roughly a quarter of pet homes. That is about 4% of all households.

steps.title: Households that pay for grooming
steps.explain: Most cats are groomed at home or not at all. Assume 30% use a paid professional at least once a year, skewed to long-haired breeds and higher incomes.

steps.title: Sessions per year
steps.explain: Paying households typically book every 3 months.

steps.title: Revenue
steps.explain: Average ticket about ₹1,200 per session including add-ons.

assumptions: Only Bangalore urban, not the wider district.
One cat per cat household on average.
Includes home visits and salons, excludes grooming products.
sanityCheck: ₹20 crore across 1.4 lakh cat homes is about ₹1,400 per cat per year, which is plausible next to ₹20,000+ yearly food spend.
